title: Language model discovers general construction rules for two previously unknown families of quantum experiments
summary: A sequence-to-sequence transformer generated readable Python meta-programs that construct photonic experimental blueprints for entire families of quantum states, rather than only individual target states. In the final paper, two successful generalizations were previously unknown: a photonic construction for general spin-1/2 states with no adjacent spin-ups, and one for states of the Majumdar–Ghosh model. The generated programs matched states beyond the three examples used as input, providing computational evidence of the inferred rules.
ai_technology: Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence language model trained on synthetic quantum-state and experimental-blueprint pairs
organization: University of Tübingen; Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light; University of Toronto; University of California, Berkeley; Stanford University; xAI

evidence.tested: A sequence-to-sequence transformer generated readable Python meta-programs that construct photonic experimental blueprints for entire families of quantum states, rather than only individual target states.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational design result, not a laboratory realization of the proposed photonic experiments. Generalization was tested by checking generated states at finite larger sizes; the authors state that arbitrary code equivalence for all system sizes is not straightforward to prove. The two constructions are counted as one paper-level discovery.
evidence.ai_role: Generated human-readable Python meta-programs from short sequences of target quantum states; the model’s programs proposed reusable experimental construction rules for whole state families, which the authors checked by simulating output states at larger system sizes.
